title: Hawaii short-term rental taxes and county rules: TAT, county TAT and GET (2026)
summary: Hawaii vacation rental taxes (11% TAT, 3% county TAT, GET), forms, filing dates and Oahu, Maui, Big Island and Kauai rules, as of November 2026.
body_markdown:
**A short-term rental in Hawaii owes three taxes on every stay: the state transient accommodations tax (TAT) at 11%, a county TAT at 3%, and the general excise tax (GET), which you can pass on to guests at up to 4.712%. The state levies them on you, the operator, and as of November 19, 2026, Airbnb doesn't collect any of them in Hawaii. On other channels, check each platform's own tax settings. On top of the taxes, each county has its own rules on where you can rent for under 30 days, and two of them changed in the last year. This guide lists every rate, form and county rule with the official source, as of November 19, 2026.**


This is a summary, not tax or legal advice. Rates and county rules in Hawaii have changed every year since 2021. Check each linked source before you file, and talk to a Hawaii tax preparer if your setup is unusual.
